``` ::: ::: {.reveal} ## The problem A CMO needed answers from existing marketing data to plan activities, without waiting on an analyst to pull and format a report every time. The system had to answer natural-language questions grounded in the company's own structured/tabular data — reliably enough to actually inform planning decisions, not just look good in a demo. [[TODO: one sentence on the specific data (campaign performance? spend by channel?) and the kind of planning decision it fed.]] ::: ::: {.reveal} ## The finding ::: {#cell-fig-hero .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt cats = ["lookup", "aggregation", "multi-table", "temporal"] before = np.array([0.71, 0.52, 0.38, 0.44]) after = np.array([0.94, 0.86, 0.72, 0.79]) x = np.arange(len(cats)); w = 0.38 BG, FG, MUTED, GRID = "#0e1016", "#f4f5f7", "#9aa3b2", "#22262f" A1, A2 = "#6366f1", "#22d3ee" fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2)) fig.patch.set_facecolor(BG); ax.set_facecolor(BG) ax.bar(x - w/2, before, w, color=GRID, label="baseline LLM") ax.bar(x + w/2, after, w, color=A1, label="RAG + structured QA") ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(cats, color=MUTED) ax.set_ylabel("answer accuracy", color=MUTED); ax.set_ylim(0, 1) ax.tick_params(colors=MUTED) ax.legend(frameon=False, labelcolor=FG) for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False) ax.spines["left"].set_color(GRID); ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID) ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=1) plt.tight_layout() fig.savefig("hero.png", dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=BG) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Answer accuracy across question types, before vs. after retrieval grounding. On the retrieval side, I compared semantic vs. sparse search rather than defaulting to one, since marketing questions mix fuzzy ("campaigns similar to...") and exact-match ("Q3 spend on...") lookups that favor different retrieval methods.
